newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia diamond giant sees De Beers deal Jan.
newsitem.headline: Russia diamond giant sees De Beers deal Jan.

text.p: Russian monopoly diamond producer, Almazy Rossii-Sakha, believes the Moscow government could approve a long-delayed export deal with South African gem giant De Beers this month, ARS's president said on Saturday.
An official for De Beers in Moscow, however, declined to endorse that forecast.
"The agreement can be signed in January and then trade relations will be resumed," ARS president Vyacheslav Shtyrov told a news conference.
But, asked to comment on Shtyrov's statement, a senior official from De Beers' Moscow office told Reuters, "I've lived in Russia too long to make predictions."
He added, "We remain a willing buyer of Russian diamonds, whatever the formal arrangments might be."
De Beers stopped all the purchases of diamonds from Russia on December 31 when it cancelled an interim arrangement after the Russian authorities failed to approve or reject a draft new trade deal.

Some senior Russian government officials said last month that the draft agreement needed reworking. They later said that Russia needed an export deal with De Beers, but have thus far failed to resolve the impasse.

De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and according to the proposed agreement Russia would deliver to De Beers 26 percent of the South African company's sales. One ARS source said on Saturday a minimum figure of $550 million of run of mine was to be included in the agreement.
Shtyrov said that several Russian ministries were making their own evaluations of the proposal.
"After this we can sign the agreement," Shtyrov said. "No one has any disagreement with the deal but we must carry out the procedure."

He added that after the agreement with De Beers, Almazy Rossii-Sakha could get loan from group of western banks to develop two new mines and two recently-discovered reserves in Russia's vast and remote Yakutia-Sakha region in Siberia.
But Shtyrov added that there was no direct link between the agreement and credit.
"If the agreement (with De Beers) were not signed then we would be looking for other investments," he said.
ARS on Saturday signed a deal with Smolensk diamond cutting plant, Russia's biggest, on supplies for three years.

Smolensk produced 195,000 carats of diamonds last year worth $150 million compared to 180,000 carats worth $185 million in 1995. The plant's director Alexander Shkadov told Reuters that after the deal with ARS the plant will produce diamonds worth $220 million in 1997. He declined to forecast a physical amount.
